result.target_summary: NVIDIA recognized an income tax expense of $4.1 billion for fiscal year 2024 (12.0% effective rate) and a benefit of $187 million for fiscal year 2023 (4.5% effective rate), with rates lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate due to FDII, stock-based compensation, and research credits.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: D060 (2024) consolidates the topics found in D066 and D068 (2023): the effective tax rate values, the comparison to the statutory rate, and the primary drivers (FDII, stock-based comp, research credits). D066 focused on the year-over-year change drivers, while D068 focused on the comparison to statutory rate. D060 combines these themes for the 2024/2023 comparison.

previous_disclosures.summary: The effective tax rate decreased from an expense of 1.9% in fiscal year 2022 to a benefit of 4.5% in fiscal year 2023, largely due to increased tax benefits from FDII, stock-based compensation, and research credits relative to lower profitability. This change was partially offset by an increase in the proportion of earnings subject to U.S. tax in 2023 and the one-time benefits from the domestication of a foreign subsidiary in 2022.

The fiscal year 2023 effective tax rate was lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% primarily due to tax benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and the U.S. federal research tax credit. This rate reflects the mandatory capitalization and amortization of R&D expenses beginning in fiscal year 2023 under the TCJA, which increased current taxes and deferred tax benefits.

comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rate
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 with a 19% effective tax rate, compared to a $346 million benefit and (68%) rate in 2023. The 2024 provision increase was driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose their income tax provision/benefit and effective tax rates for fiscal year 2024. NVIDIA reported an expense of $4.1 billion with a 12.0% effective rate, attributing the rate increase to decreased impacts from FDII, stock-based compensation, and R&D credits relative to income growth. In contrast, AMD reported a much smaller provision of $381 million with a 19% effective rate, driven by higher pre-tax income and a specific $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction. While both companies cite R&D and stock-based compensation as factors influencing their rates, AMD's 2024 rate was significantly higher than NVIDIA's, and AMD's provision was heavily impacted by a one-time integration transaction, whereas NVIDIA's change was driven by relative shifts in permanent benefits against growing income.

sentences.text: We recognized income tax expense of $4.1 billion for fiscal year 2024 and income tax benefit of $187 million for fiscal year 2023.

The effective tax rate increased due to a decreased impact of tax benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and the U.S. federal research tax credit, relative to the increase in income before income tax.
We recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2023, representing effective tax rates of 19% and (68%), respectively.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidate disclosures (D050, D051) focus on increases in R&D and SG&A expenses driven by the VMware Merger and headcount, not income tax provisions or effective tax rates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance and effective tax rate change
comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets in 2024. This allowance was recognized in the third quarter of 2024 after determining it was more likely than not that the assets would not be recoverable, largely due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position resulting from asset impairment and restructuring charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Intel discuss the drivers behind their 2024 effective tax rate changes. NVIDIA attributes its increase to a decreased impact of specific tax benefits (FDII, SBC, R&D credits) relative to income growth. Intel, conversely, attributes its rate increase primarily to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position. Both companies identify distinct structural or operational reasons for the rate movement, with NVIDIA reflecting profitability-driven normalization and Intel reflecting a negative allowance adjustment due to past losses.

sentences.text: The effective tax rate increased due to a decreased impact of tax benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and the U.S. federal research tax credit, relative to the increase in income before income tax.

Our effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by the effects associated with the establishment of a valuation allowance against our US federal deferred tax assets in 2024.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Substantially all of QCOM's income is taxed in the U.S., with a significant portion qualifying for preferential treatment as FDII at a 13% effective tax rate. comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Qualcomm (QCOM) explicitly cite the Foreign-Derived Intangible Income (FDII) deduction as a key factor driving their effective tax rates below the U.S. statutory rate. NVIDIA states its 2024 rate was lower than 21% due to FDII, stock-based compensation, and research credits. Similarly, QCOM notes that a significant portion of its U.S. taxed income qualifies for FDII preferential treatment at a 13% effective rate. Both disclosures highlight FDII as a major component of their tax expense calculations.
